message.content:
The input cell is rhombohedral-like in its raw setting: all three edge lengths coincide at [[param:cell.a]], [[param:cell.b]], and [[param:cell.c]], while the interaxial angles are given by [[param:cell.alpha]], [[param:cell.beta]], and the distinctly smaller [[param:cell.gamma]], so the two larger angles match each other but the third is measurably different. This primitive-looking cell holds three atoms in total ([[param:input.atom_count]]), comprising one krypton ([[param:composition.Kr]]) and two fluorines ([[param:composition.F]]).

The symmetry assigned to the structure is space group number [[param:space_group.number]] with Hall symbol [[param:space_group.hall]], a body-centered tetragonal group. To express the input cell in that conventional I-centered tetragonal setting, a change of basis is applied: the transformation matrix [[param:frame.matrix]] maps input fractional coordinates into the standard frame, accompanied by the origin shift [[param:frame.origin_shift]], which is zero in all three components, so the two frames share the same origin and differ only in the choice of lattice vectors. Input fractional coordinates were handled at a working precision of [[param:round_digits]] decimal places.

Within the standard setting, the three input atoms resolve into two independent Wyckoff orbits. The krypton sublattice is represented by orbit [[param:orbit.o000.id]], whose element is [[param:orbit.o000.element]] occupying the Wyckoff site [[param:orbit.o000.wyckoff]]. This site has no free positional parameters: its atoms sit at the fixed special position 0, 0, 0, with the body-centering of the lattice generating the second member of the multiplicity-two orbit.

The fluorine sublattice forms orbit [[param:orbit.o001.id]], with element [[param:orbit.o001.element]] on the Wyckoff site [[param:orbit.o001.wyckoff]]. This fourfold orbit lies on the coordinate line 0, 0, z and possesses a single free parameter along the c direction, given by [[param:orbit.o001.parameters]]; the four members of the orbit are generated from this one degree of freedom by the tetragonal symmetry operations combined with the I-centering translation.

No precision corrections were required: the reported atomic positions coincide with the idealized symmetry description, so the structure as given is already an exact realization of the two-orbit arrangement in this space group.
